case_studies.title: Socio-Technical Anti-Patterns in Building ML-Enabled Software: Insights from Leaders on the Forefront
case_studies.abstract: Although machine learning (ML)-enabled software systems seem to be a success story considering their rise in economic power, there are consistent reports from companies and practitioners struggling to bring ML models into production. Many papers have focused on specific, and purely technical aspects, such as testing and pipelines, but only few on socio-technical aspects. Driven by numerous anecdotes and reports from practitioners, our goal is to collect and analyze socio-technical challenges of productionizing ML models centered around and within teams. To this end, we conducted the largest qu
case_studies.summary: This research identifies socio-technical challenges that companies face when deploying machine learning models into production, aiming to help teams overcome these hurdles. The authors interviewed leaders and collected insights on the struggles of productionizing ML models. The result is a better understanding of the non-technical issues that hinder successful ML model deployment.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage machine learning model deployment, here is what to do: review your team's collaboration and communication processes, assess the alignment of technical and business goals, and identify potential socio-technical roadblocks that may be hindering successful model production. This flags a risk: if your org uses ML models, check for potential team and process bottlenecks immediately. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant for those involved in ML model deployment.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: IT-relevant socio-technical anti-patterns, Real-world impact: May impact software development teams' practices, Maturity: Basic analysis of ML challenges, Monetisation: No clear path for consultants. Raising the bar for the 'IT-Relevance' score due to the lack of direct impact on tooling or systems used in infrastructure.

case_studies.title: ToolAlignBench: Investigating Alignment Conflicts in Tool-Calling Enabled LLMs
case_studies.abstract: Safety alignment in LLMs aims to align models with human values, but which values take precedence when they conflict? We investigate this question in the context of tool-calling LLM agents deployed in regulated industries, where agents processing confidential documents may encounter content that triggers safety-trained values (e.g., public welfare) that conflict with deployment-context instructions (e.g., internal logging). To empirically verify this phenomenon, we build a benchmark of 128 scenarios across 16 domains. We find that safety-aligned open-source models override their deployment ins
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of alignment conflicts in large language models, where human values may clash with deployment instructions. The researchers built a benchmark of 128 scenarios to investigate this issue in tool-calling enabled LLMs. The result showed that safety-aligned models can override their deployment instructions in certain situations.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on the development and safety of large language models rather than cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.relevance_tag: LLM tool-calling agents in regulated industries
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: LLM tool-calling agents are of increasing interest to IT engineers. The abstract hints at new information about how safety-trained values in LLMs conflict. IT Relevance: Given IT engineer's use of LLM agents in regulated industries, this paper is somewhat relevant. Value 90 days: An IT engineer could apply the insights from this paper to mitigate potential safety risks in their own deployments, potentially within 90 days.

case_studies.title: On-Policy Delta Distillation
case_studies.abstract: On-policy distillation is an alternative post-training method in reinforcement learning that alleviates the constraints imposed by reward models by providing token-level supervision from a teacher model. Although on-policy distillation has been studied and applied across various settings, its fundamental design remains underexplored. In this paper, we introduce a new distillation reward, termed the delta signal, instead of directly imitating the teacher's output distribution. The delta signal is defined as the difference between the teacher model and its base model prior to instruction tuning
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited reinforcement learning by introducing a new distillation reward called the delta signal, which allows for more efficient learning from a teacher model. The authors built a new on-policy distillation method using this delta signal. The result is a more effective way to train models in certain settings.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it relates to reinforcement learning and model training, which is typically handled by data science or machine learning teams.
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper introduces a new concept in reinforcement learning, on-policy delta distillation, which has some novelty and relevance to the IT field, particularly in AI deployment. However, its applicability to real-world IT infrastructure within 90 days is limited. The low monetisation potential score aligns with the lack of concrete, deployable ideas. The total score is above 40, but the 'real_world_impact' is relatively low, indicating an uncertain real-world relevance.

case_studies.title: AI-Native Insurance for Agentic AI: Pricing, Underwriting, and End-to-End Automation
case_studies.abstract: Agentic AI introduces new insurance challenges because autonomous AI systems can make decisions, invoke tools, modify external environments, and interact with third-party services. This paper develops an AI-native mathematical framework for underwriting, pricing, and contract design for agentic AI deployments. A deployment is represented by a risk state that captures autonomy level, operational authority, permission exposure, governance maturity, and dependency concentration. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of insuring autonomous AI systems by developing a mathematical framework for underwriting and pricing AI-native insurance contracts. The researchers built an AI-native framework that maps risk states to event probabilities and premiums. The result provides a way to automate insurance processes for agentic AI deployments.
case_studies.it_breakdown: This is not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, but it may be relevant for IT teams responsible for managing autonomous AI systems to be aware of the emerging insurance solutions for these systems. If your organisation uses autonomous AI, this research may inform your conversations with insurance providers. It does not require immediate action from IT infrastructure managers.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: The concept of insurance for agentic AI is new, but the approach is largely within the realm of traditional actuarial science. Novelty is somewhat mitigated by its low IT relevance. IT Relevance: Scores low, as this work focuses on the theoretical development of insurance for agentic AI, with limited consideration of IT infrastructure. case_studies.title: ARMOR++: Agentic Orchestration of a Multi-Domain Primitive Set for Transferable Attacks on Deepfake Detectors
case_studies.abstract: The reliability of deepfake detectors frequently degrades under black-box adversarial transfer, as these models often rely on fragile, architecture-dependent forensic cues. Existing transfer attacks often lack semantic awareness and struggle to maintain effectiveness under strict no-query constraints, particularly when perturbations are transferred from convolutional surrogates to transformer-based targets. To address these limitations, this paper introduces ARMOR++, a robust multi-agent framework designed for high-transferability deepfake evasion. The framework leverages the Qwen2.5-VL Vision
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of deepfake detectors being unreliable under black-box adversarial transfer by building a robust multi-agent framework called ARMOR++, which results in high-transferability deepfake evasion. The framework leverages a set of primitives to improve the effectiveness of transfer attacks. This research is not directly relevant to cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on improving the robustness of deepfake detectors and developing transfer attacks, which is more relevant to AI and cybersecurity research. If your organization uses deepfake detection models, this research may be of interest from a security perspective. No immediate action is required for cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Academic novelty but no direct IT relevance; no actionable IT advice.

case_studies.title: MM-IssueLoc: A Controlled Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Evidence in Multimodal Repository-Level Issue Localization
case_studies.abstract: Real repository issues routinely include visual evidence such as screenshots, error dialogs, rendered UI states, and logs, yet repository-level issue localization is evaluated mostly as a text-only task. Existing multimodal SE benchmarks evaluate end-to-end repair, entangling localization with patch synthesis and obscuring whether visual input helped, hurt, or was ignored. We introduce \textbf{MM-IssueLoc}, a controlled benchmark and evaluation protocol for repository-level localization with visual evidence. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating visual evidence in issue localization by building a controlled benchmark called MM-IssueLoc, which provides a dataset of 652 issue-PR instances across 23 languages. The result is a more accurate evaluation of repository-level issue localization with visual evidence. This research is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on evaluating visual evidence in issue localization for software development. If your organization is involved in software development research, this benchmark may be of interest. Otherwise, no action is required.
